QF.id: AIFM CII Fund Performance and Benchmarking_24

question.text: Ms. Kavita Joshi is the Key Investment Professional of Arjuna Growth AIF (Cat II). Her sudden resignation triggers the 'key-person event' clause in the PPM. Which of the following is the typical LP-protective mechanism?

answer.text: Automatic wind-up of the fund within 30 days.
Conversion of the Cat II AIF into a Cat III AIF.
Automatic doubling of the management fee to retain remaining team.
Suspension of investment period and capital calls for new investments until a replacement is approved by the LPAC / supermajority of LPs.

explanation.text: The Logic: Industry-standard key-person clauses suspend further investment-period capital calls and fresh investments until LPs (often LPAC or a supermajority) approve a replacement key professional. Already-made investments continue; the fund is not force-wound-up but frozen from new deployments. This protects LPs from 'orphaned capital' under an unfamiliar manager. The Trap: Auto-wind-up (A) is extreme and rare. Doubling fees (C) is anti-LP. Category switching (B) requires fresh SEBI application. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-C tests the same mechanic for all-Cat managers. XXI-B PMS has analogous key-person representations but typically less formal suspension mechanics. Manager's Pro-Tip: Draft the key-person clause with a 90-day 'grace cure period' before suspension triggers — this protects against opportunistic LP withdrawal if a non-critical team change happens. Specify named individuals (not just titles) to avoid ambiguity.
